headline: Highest risk is medium: Dify can write and execute server-side code while PaddleOCR processes documents, creating shared-workspace leakage and output-trust risks; no critical pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and run shell/subprocesses, so if PaddleOCR outputs are placed into the shared Dify datastore or files, attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions. PaddleOCR is a document processor with browser/API surfaces, but no direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR outputs are ingested into Dify prompts or workflow variables without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF both agents exchange content through the Dify server datastore, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Sanitize OCR text before inserting it into Dify prompts.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction wrapper around all PaddleOCR outputs.
Route OCR output through a validation step that strips control-like phrases.
Disable automatic reuse of prior conversation or datastore content for prompt assembly.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs and can write/read files; PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If the same workspace or datastore is shared, document contents can flow into Dify logs or outputs. No evidence shows local-only isolation for the pair, so the shared-data pathway is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF documents processed by PaddleOCR are stored in the same workspace Dify reads from, leakage is possible.
IF Dify logs or conversation history include OCR text, sensitive document content can persist.
mitigations: Store OCR inputs and Dify logs in separate directories.
Turn off or minimize conversation logging for document jobs.
Redact sensitive fields before passing OCR output onward.
Restrict file permissions on shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad filesystem write and shell execution, while PaddleOCR has browser and allowlisted network egress. Even without explicit git or DB writes, both can mutate shared files or shared workflow artifacts if orchestrated together. Because the shared-state mechanism is documented for Dify but not the exact pair, uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or artifact directory, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
IF PaddleOCR browser/API steps and Dify shell steps target the same files, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Make one agent read-only on shared artifacts.
Use timestamped output filenames to avoid overwrite.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can act as an orchestrator and execute tools, so if it consumes PaddleOCR text as authoritative without verification, OCR mistakes can cascade into downstream actions or generated content. PaddleOCR is not a verifier; it only extracts from documents/images. The pair therefore has a default trust-chain risk, though not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF Dify uses PaddleOCR output directly in prompts or tool inputs without validation, errors propagate.
IF downstream workflows trigger actions based on OCR text, misreads can become operational mistakes.
mitigations: Add a human review step for extracted fields.
Require confidence thresholds before downstream actions.
Cross-check critical values against the source document image.
Log OCR provenance alongside each extracted field.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for OCR outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge base content, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If those documents contain regulated data, retention and residency obligations can diverge because Dify stores conversational artifacts and PaddleOCR is unverified on compliance controls. The pair creates a plausible policy mismatch, but no specific residency breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through both agents, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF Dify logs OCR-derived content longer than the source system permits, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Classify document jobs by data sensitivity before processing.
Shorten or disable retention for OCR workflows.
Avoid sending regulated fields into conversation logs.
Document a shared retention policy for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement.
